title: Root on the bottom
summary: Stacked in 3rds from the root: the layout you already know.

steps.title: Root position
steps.body:
When the root is the lowest note, a chord is in **root position**. Every triad you built in Unit 4 was in root position: C E G, with C at the bottom.

**Why it matters:** Root position sounds the most solid and settled. It is the layout to fall back on, and the one other layouts are named against.

steps.title: G in root position
steps.body: G at the bottom, then B, then D.

items.prompt: Play a C major triad in root position.
Play an A minor triad in root position.

steps.title: Check the bottom
steps.body: Play any chord you know and look at the lowest key. If it is the root, the chord is in root position.

items.prompt: Is this chord in root position?
Is this chord in root position?
Play a G major triad in root position.
